subject: science
chapter_title: Patterns in Life: Diversity and Classification

concepts.title: Biodiversity - The Variety of Life
concepts.definition: The earth is home to an enormous variety of life forms, from microscopic organisms invisible to the naked eye to giant trees; this biodiversity includes plants that survive long droughts and insects that protect or damage crops, and India is one of the world's megadiverse countries.
concepts.key_idea: Life's variety spans sizes and habitats - biodiversity is the planet's living library.
question_patterns: what is biodiversity - define with examples
why do different organisms live in different habitats
name two factors that make an area biodiverse

solution_steps.explain: Biodiversity covers the range of organisms from microbes to trees.
Different climates and landscapes host different life forms.
Each species plays a role in ecosystems and human welfare.

concepts.title: Classification - Grouping by Characteristics
concepts.definition: The study of biological diversity becomes possible through classification - a systematic framework that groups organisms by shared characteristics, from ancient traditions like the Sangam Tinai classification of landscapes to modern scientific taxonomy.
concepts.key_idea: Group by traits: classification turns a crowd of species into an ordered library.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc112.txt sections on classification and its history
question_patterns: what is classification - why is it needed
on what basis are plants and animals classified

solution_steps.explain: Body design, cell structure and habitat guide grouping.
Broad groups split into finer ones as traits accumulate.
Each organism finds one place in the scheme.

concepts.title: Hierarchy of Classification: Kingdom to Species
concepts.definition: Modern classification arranges organisms in ranks - kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species - narrowing from broad body plans to closely related groups; the two-kingdom scheme of plants and animals has grown into five kingdoms covering monera, protista, fungi, plantae and animalia.
concepts.key_idea: Kingdom to species: each rank narrows the circle of relatives.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc112.txt sections on hierarchy, kingdoms and organ systems

solution_steps.explain: Kingdom down to species forms a narrowing ladder.
Cell type, body organisation and organ systems decide each level.
Walk the ladder to reach the species name.
